description: Backend: add three JWT-authorized admin routes for a single quiz (GET/PUT/DELETE /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}) and tighten CORS to the Amplify domain, end-to-end (API Gateway preflight AND Lambda response header). Implement handler logic + a shared prefix-delete helper in lambda/index.ts, wire the routes to the existing HttpJwtAuthorizer in lib/quiz-app-stack.ts with allowMethods extended to PUT/DELETE and a parameterized allowedOrigin, and update both test files. Independent of FEAT-002 (docs).
steps: lambda/index.ts: Add an exported pure validator for the EDIT body. The edit is full-replace and the quizId comes from the PATH, so a new pure helper `validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate(input, quizId)` should validate/normalize {title, questions[]} using the SAME per-question validation rules as validateAndNormalizeQuizInput (title non-empty trimmed; questions non-empty array; each question text non-empty trimmed; options >=2 all non-empty trimmed; answerIndex integer within range), and return { ok:true, quiz: NormalizedQuiz } with quiz.quizId set to the given path quizId (do NOT auto-generate, do NOT read quizId from the body). Return { ok:false, error } on failure. Refactor the shared per-question validation out of validateAndNormalizeQuizInput into a small internal helper so both entry points share it and stay in sync (keep validateAndNormalizeQuizInput's existing exported signature and behavior, including quizId auto-generation, unchanged so existing tests still pass).

lambda/index.ts: Add a shared async helper to delete all items for a quiz, e.g. `deleteQuizItems(quizId: string): Promise<void>`. DocumentClient has no prefix delete: first learn the keys (reuse getQuizItems, or Query pk=QUIZ#<quizId>) to collect every {pk, sk} (the META item AND all Q#n items), then BatchWrite DeleteRequests in chunks of <=25 with the SAME UnprocessedItems bounded-retry pattern used in writeQuizItems/seedSampleData. Keep single-table key shapes identical (pk=`QUIZ#${quizId}`, sk='META' or `Q#${n}`).

lambda/index.ts: Add handler branches (dispatch on event.routeKey), mirroring the existing 'POST /api/admin/quizzes' audit-log style (read Cognito claims from event.requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims and console.log the caller sub/username):
- 'GET /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}': require quizId (400 if missing); getQuizItems; 404 {message:'quiz not found'} if no meta; return 200 with the quiz INCLUDING answerIndex on each question (do NOT call toPublicQuestions). Return questions sorted by n with fields {n,text,options,answerIndex}.
- 'PUT /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}': require quizId (400); parse body (400 {message:'invalid JSON body'} on parse error); validate via validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate(parsed, quizId) (400 {message:error} on failure); getQuizItems and 404 {message:'quiz not found'} if the quiz does not already exist (edit, not create); then FULL-REPLACE: deleteQuizItems(quizId) followed by writeQuizItems(normalizedQuiz) so META.questionCount and Q#n items reflect the new payload exactly. Return 200 with {quizId, title, questionCount}.
- 'DELETE /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}': require quizId (400); getQuizItems and 404 {message:'quiz not found'} if no meta (consistent with create route's existence checks); deleteQuizItems(quizId); return 200 with {quizId, deleted:true} (or 204-style 200 body; pick one and keep it consistent).

lambda/index.ts: Make the CORS response header coherent with a single allowed origin. Replace the hardcoded `'access-control-allow-origin': '*'` in JSON_HEADERS with the value from an env var, e.g. `process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (falling back to '*' if unset so local/dev still works). Read it in the json() helper (or build headers per-response) so every response returns the configured origin. The stack (next steps) sets this env var on the Lambda to the same allowedOrigin used for API Gateway CORS.

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: Introduce a configurable allowed origin following the existing override patterns in this stack. Add a CDK context value OR CfnParameter named `allowedOrigin` with DEFAULT 'https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com'. Prefer a synth-time CDK context value (this.node.tryGetContext('allowedOrigin') ?? 'https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com') so it can be used directly in both the CORS allowOrigins array AND the Lambda environment (a CfnParameter token cannot be safely placed in a JS string array element for allowOrigins, and the stack test asserts the literal domain in the synthesized template, so a synth-time context string is the clean choice). Update the corsPreflight block: allowOrigins: [allowedOrigin]; allowMethods must include GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS (add PUT and DELETE); keep allowHeaders ['content-type','authorization']. Update the surrounding comment that currently justifies '*'.
lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: Pass the allowed origin to the Lambda so its response header matches. Add ALLOWED_ORIGIN: allowedOrigin to the apiFunction environment map (next to TABLE_NAME).

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: Register the three new admin routes on httpApi via addRoutes, each with `authorizer: adminJwtAuthorizer` (the SAME existing HttpJwtAuthorizer used by POST /api/admin/quizzes), sharing the existing `integration`:
- path '/api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}', methods [GET]
- path '/api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}', methods [PUT]
- path '/api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}', methods [DELETE]
Leave the three public routes (GET /api/quizzes, GET /api/quizzes/{quizId}, POST /api/quizzes/{quizId}/submit) OPEN and unchanged, and leave POST /api/admin/quizzes unchanged.

test/handler.test.ts: Add a describe block for validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate covering: valid input normalizes and sets quiz.quizId to the passed path id (ignoring any quizId in the body); rejects non-object body; rejects missing/empty title; rejects empty/missing questions array; rejects a question with <2 options; rejects empty option strings; rejects out-of-range/non-integer answerIndex; confirms a body-supplied quizId does NOT override the path quizId. Keep using the REAL exported function (no mocks).

test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts: Update route assertions. Change the 'defines the four expected routes' test to expect SEVEN routes (3 public + POST admin create + GET/PUT/DELETE admin single-quiz) and assert each RouteKey exists: add 'GET /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}', 'PUT /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}', 'DELETE /api/admin/quizzes/{quizId}'. Add assertions that each of the three new admin routes has AuthorizationType 'JWT' with AuthorizerId Match.anyValue() (bound to the JWT authorizer). Keep the 'public routes have no authorizer' test unchanged and passing. Add/adjust the CORS test to assert CorsConfiguration.AllowOrigins equals ['https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com'] (specifically NOT containing '*') and AllowMethods includes PUT and DELETE (Match.arrayWith(['GET','POST','PUT','DELETE','OPTIONS'])). Keep resourceCountIs for Authorizer at 1 (same authorizer reused).
acceptance_criteria: lambda/index.ts exports validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate and handles the three new routeKeys with full-replace edit, answerIndex-inclusive admin read, and delete, all with 404 on missing quiz and json(status,{message}) error shapes.
The admin read route returns answerIndex on each question; the public GET /api/quizzes/{quizId} still strips it (unchanged).
deleteQuizItems removes META + all Q#n items via BatchWrite DeleteRequests (<=25) with UnprocessedItems retry, keeping key shapes identical.

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts registers the 3 new routes bound to the existing adminJwtAuthorizer; allowMethods include PUT and DELETE; allowOrigins is [the Amplify domain] via a configurable allowedOrigin defaulting to https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com; the Lambda gets ALLOWED_ORIGIN set to the same value.
The public routes and POST /api/admin/quizzes remain open/unchanged respectively; only one JWT authorizer exists.

test/handler.test.ts covers validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate; test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts asserts 7 routes, the 3 new routes JWT-bound, public routes open, and CORS allowOrigins is the specific domain with PUT/DELETE in allowMethods.
No new idle-cost resources; DynamoDB stays PAY_PER_REQUEST; no VPC/NAT added.
verification: Read-based in sandbox (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY): confirm handler routeKeys exactly match the stack route paths+methods; confirm allowOrigins literal equals the Amplify domain in both stack and Lambda env; confirm delete helper reuses the <=25 UnprocessedItems retry pattern and identical key shapes.
On the user's networked host: `npm ci && npm run build && npm test && npx cdk synth` must all pass (build clean, all jest tests green including new ones, synth succeeds).
findings: Implemented in lambda/index.ts, lib/quiz-app-stack.ts and both test files. Refactored the shared per-question/title validation out of validateAndNormalizeQuizInput into an internal validateTitleAndQuestions helper; added exported validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate(input, quizId) that sets quizId from the path (ignores any body quizId, never auto-generates) and reuses the same rules. Added deleteQuizItems(quizId) that learns keys via getQuizItems then BatchWrite DeleteRequests in <=25 chunks with the same UnprocessedItems bounded-retry pattern; key shapes identical (pk=QUIZ#<id>, sk=META|Q#<n>). Added GET (answerIndex-inclusive, no toPublicQuestions) / PUT (404 if missing, full-replace delete+write) / DELETE (404 if missing) handler branches, all with json(status,{message}) error shapes and a shared logAdminCaller audit-log helper (also now used by the existing POST create route). Lambda access-control-allow-origin now comes from process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGIN (fallback '*'). Stack: added synth-time context allowedOrigin (this.node.tryGetContext('allowedOrigin') ?? 'https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com') used in corsPreflight.allowOrigins:[allowedOrigin] and Lambda env ALLOWED_ORIGIN; added PUT+DELETE to allowMethods (kept GET/POST/OPTIONS, allowHeaders content-type/authorization); registered the 3 new routes on the existing adminJwtAuthorizer; updated the stale '*'-justifying comment. Tests: added validateAndNormalizeQuizUpdate describe block; stack test now expects 7 routes, asserts the 3 new admin routes JWT-bound, public routes still open, CorsConfiguration.AllowOrigins === ['https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com'] (and NOT containing '*'), AllowMethods include PUT/DELETE, Lambda ALLOWED_ORIGIN env matches, Authorizer count kept at 1. VERIFICATION: sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY with no node_modules and npm registry 403, so tsc/jest/cdk synth could NOT be run here; changes were authored correct-by-construction and verified by reading (routeKeys match stack paths+methods, delete retry pattern + key shapes verified, literal origin verified in both places). The user must run `npm ci && npm run build && npm test && npx cdk synth` on their networked host to confirm build/tests/synth are green. No new idle-cost resources; DynamoDB stays PAY_PER_REQUEST; no VPC/NAT.
